Therefore the pool can be regarded as a rectangle with length 50 m and width w. Reasoning: Sarah swims six "lengths," each length is 50 m, so Sarah's distance is 6×50=300 m. Ruth runs around the perimeter of the pool; the perimeter of the rectangle is 2(50+w), and she runs 5 laps, so the distance is 5×2(50+w). Thus 10(50+w)=900, 50+w=90, so w=40. The pool width is 40 m.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a rectangular pool with length 50 m and unknown width w. From the text, Sarah swims six lengths, so her distance is 6×50 = 300 m. Ruth runs five perimeters, so her distance is 5×2(50+w). Since Ruth runs three times as fast as Sarah but they take the same time, Ruth must cover three times Sarah's distance: 5×2(50+w)=3×300. Solve 10(50+w)=900, so 50+w=90 and w=40 m.
